name: How to Read the Evidence in This Volume
title: How to Read the Evidence in This Volume
answer: This idea explains how to read the evidence labels attached to the 300 ideas in this volume. It says most ideas are labeled Practice, meaning they are informed judgment rather than proven method, so schools should treat them with appropriate caution. The labels help readers decide how much risk to accept and when to check back as research changes.

crumbs.name: What AI Can and Cannot Do

sections.body: The volume gives every idea an evidence label so readers can tell whether it has been tested or is a sensible practice not yet studied. Both kinds of ideas are included, but they require different levels of caution. Figure 1.7 defines the four labels and shows how many ideas carry each. Most ideas fall under Practice, which the text says is not a weakness to hide. Generative AI arrived in schools in late 2022, and careful research takes years, so much current AI use rests on judgment rather than proven method.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: The text does not give grade bands for this idea, so the habits apply across a school or classroom. First, start small and measure something that matters, such as learning, time saved, or attendance, rather than only whether people liked the tool, and Chapter 4 explains how. Second, favor ideas where the risk is low if the idea does not work, such as drafting a newsletter. Avoid ideas where a mistake could hurt a child, such as flagging students for discipline. Third, check back, because research is moving fast and some labels in the volume may change soon after publication.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text states that every one of the 300 ideas in this volume carries an evidence label. Figure 1.7 defines the four labels and shows how many ideas carry each. It also states that most of the ideas are labeled Practice. The text does not report a study, number, or finding beyond that label and figure. It says careful research takes years and that most current AI practice in schools is informed judgment, not proven method.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The text says both tested ideas and untested practices belong in the volume, but they call for different levels of caution. Because most ideas are labeled Practice, they should be treated as informed judgment rather than proven method. The text advises starting small, measuring something that matters, and favoring low-risk uses over high-risk ones. It gives the example of drafting a newsletter as low risk and flagging students for discipline as a case where a mistake could hurt a child. It also says readers should check back, since research is moving fast and some labels may change soon after publication.
